ideas.label: Triangulation
ideas.principle: Lose a tempo without changing the essential position.
ideas.summary: Triangulation is a controlled loss of tempo: the king uses three moves to return to the same square while forcing the opponent to move. Use it only after identifying the desired zugzwang.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]

ideas.label: Triangulation
ideas.principle: Treat spare pawn moves as tempi, not automatic improvements.
ideas.summary: Count reserve pawn tempi before triangulating. A harmless pawn move may decide who must yield the opposition, but pushing too soon can remove a square your own king needs.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]

ideas.label: Triangulation
ideas.principle: Preserve the king's triangulation squares when fixing the pawn structure.
ideas.summary: In king-and-pawn endings, triangulate only when the returning king move hands the opponent the same position with the move. Confirm that the pawn has enough reserve tempi and does not occupy a key square such as e4 that the king needs for the maneuver.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]
